summary: Duplicate ephemeral API key accounting during cross-region tenant migration causing intermittent 429 throttles
description:
Issue summary: During a scheduled cross-region tenant migration for Vectra Health (dedicated pool), multiple ephemeral API keys were created by the customer's migration utility. The rate-limiter observed duplicate registrations for logically identical ephemeral sessions which caused the tenant's token-account to be over-counted, resulting in intermittent 429 throttles for short-lived streams and small embedding batches.

Impact: Several of Vectra's ingestion workers experienced short (1–3 minute) bursts of 429 responses during the migration window on 2026-03-10, causing queue backpressure and retries. No data loss observed; impact was degraded ingest throughput and elevated client error rates (5–7% of requests during spikes).

Environment: prod-us-east (dedicated pool), edge proxies in us-east-1 and failover path to us-west-2. Affected models include redwood/gpt-large-v1 for streaming and redwood/embedding-encoder-v2 for embedding batches.

Observed behavior: Edge token accounting and central quota-engine counters became briefly inconsistent after a Redis replica promotion during the migration. The migration tool (tenant-migrator v2) opened ephemeral sessions with fresh keys while the edge cache had stale token-bucket state; when the central quota reconciler ran it double-counted the new keys as additional concurrent usage, pushing the tenant over the short-term concurrency window and emitting 429s.

Why this is different from a normal quota spike: This is not a pure traffic surge — the same number of logical sessions existed, but registration of duplicates across edge and control-plane caches caused the accounting delta. It manifested as short bursts tied to the migration steps (key issuance + cache invalidate).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use tenant-migrator v2 to create ephemeral keys while simultaneously promoting a Redis replica (simulate failover)
2) Immediately start multiple short-lived streaming sessions (100-200 concurrent, <30s each) against the dedicated pool
3) Observe token-bucket counts at the edge (edge-proxy logs) vs central quota-engine (quota service metrics) and watch for temporary over-counts and 429 responses
4) Verify that turning off the reconciler or delaying key-registration reduces the duplicate counting and eliminates the 429 bursts
logs: 2026-03-10T11:03:21Z rate-limiter INFO token_bucket: tenant=vectra key=ephemeral-xyz count=0 last_refill=2026-03-10T11:02:50Z
2026-03-10T11:03:22Z quota-engine WARN reconcile: detected +198 delta between edge_count=372 and central_count=570 for tenant=vectra
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: traffic surge from customer workers — disproved: client-side logs show steady ingest rate, bursts align with migration steps.
Found correlation between Redis replica promotion (2026-03-10T11:02:58Z) and spike in duplicate ephemeral key registrations in edge cache.
Edge cache TTL reset allowed new key registration to skip dedupe path; central reconciler counted both old and new registrations during its 60s reconciliation window.
Temporary mitigation: increased reconciliation dedupe window and added a short-lived suppressor (30s) to ignore immediate duplicate registrations from the same client IP during migrations.

Long-term fix: patch quota-engine to detect ephemeral key lineage and perform idempotent registration (PR linked). Scheduled follow-up: infra PR to add stronger idempotency headers from tenant-migrator v2.
Observed after mitigation: 429 spikes reduced to <0.2% for a subsequent migration test run.
Related telemetry: token-bucket-compare dashboard (confluence link attached) shows the pre/post delta and time alignment with Redis failover events.

resolution: Mitigation applied: reconciliation dedupe window increased and a short suppressor was added to reduce immediate duplicate registration counts. Permanent fix: quota-engine idempotency patch (PR 4021) to be rolled out in next deploy. Follow-up: publish migration best-practices doc and add a small delay/retry in tenant-migrator to avoid simultaneous key issuance during Redis failover.
next_steps: 1) Merge and deploy PR 4021 for idempotent ephemeral key registration
2) Add a telemetry alert that fires when edge/central token count delta > 20% for >30s
3) Publish a short runbook for customers performing tenant migrations recommending staggered key issuance and a 45s quiesce window during Redis promotions
4) Coordinate with Vectra to validate the fix during their next scheduled migration
